articles.title: Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second
articles.summary: Who can stop Brighton’s ascension in English and European football? They continue to set standards, practices that leave almost everybody else trailing in their wake. Their second-place position in the Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a Football Manager session.
body: Come November 2026, they appear the only team capable of throwing down a challenge to Arsenal. Under low winter sun, Brentford, the club Brighton are often compared to, though one with a different outlook, were readily swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’ team, and their fans at the Amex, might level blame at a couple of refereeing decisions, it was a contest they were given little chance of rescuing anything from.

A successful return to the Amex following five Brighton away trips, more than 5,000 miles on the road including victory at Manchester City and Getafe over the last two outings. Normal service was duly resumed, any negatives coming in a failure to add to their first-half goals. Brentford returned to a stadium where they have never won in the Premier League.

articles.title: Alcaraz exacts revenge on Shelton to win Paris Masters
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz avenged his US Open defeat to Ben Shelton with a 7-6(7-5) 7-5 victory, claiming his maiden Paris Masters title in straight sets.
body: Alcaraz edged a thrilling opening set, roaring towards the Paris crowd after clinching the tie-break. Neither player could find a breakthrough in a set lasting 65 minutes, with Shelton unable to convert any of his six break-point opportunities.

The second set looked to be taking a similar course of action until Shelton shocked Alcaraz with a break to love at 3-2, firing two aces past his opponent in the game, but Alcaraz bounced back with a break at the earliest opportunity to bring the scores back to level at 4-4.
The world No 3 seized the momentum, firing up the crowd before producing a stunning winner off a Shelton drop shot to secure the crucial break, take the second set 7-5 and claim the championship.

Alcaraz's maiden Paris title marks his ninth consecutive match win and fifth tournament victory from six finals in 2026. It also exacts revenge on Shelton, who beat him in a gruelling 4hr 28min US Open quarter-final in September.

articles.title: Tepid Chelsea beaten by Sunderland who move off bottom
articles.summary: Chelsea put in a tepid performance as Sunderland lifted themselves off the bottom of the Premier League table with a 1-0 win that eases the pressure on under-fire manager Regis Le Bris.
body: Xabi Alonso's side were second-best throughout. None of their midfield attack won a duel or a tackle in the opening 20 minutes, while Sunderland's fight was best shown through Brian Brobbey's efforts up front.
The Dutch international smashed his way through Chelsea centre-backs Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill in a brutal first half - coming close to scoring twice, before eventually getting his rewards.
Ten minutes before half-time, he rolled past Colwill with immense strength to win a penalty, which Enzo Le Fee converted. Colwill was then taken off at half-time.

If Chelsea were weak in defence, they weren't much better in attack. They struggled to break down a Sunderland defence that has been leaking goals of late. Morgan Rogers went closest in the first half with an off-target header, while their only chance of note in the second half was Danny Welbeck's injury-time miss.

articles.title: Sage in big trouble as Palace hit rock-bottom after defeat to Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to inflict a fourth consecutive Premier League defeat on the hosts and leave Pierre Sage in a perilous position with his side bottom of the table.
body: Palace substitute Eddie Nketiah pulled a goal back from the spot with the last kick of the game, but the damage was already done after Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz struck for Liverpool either side of half time and Alexander Isak added a third late on.

Liverpool secured a much-needed result following back-to-back defeats at Arsenal and Fenerbahce. The victory, their first for three games in all competitions, moves Liverpool up to fourth in the table.

Goalkeeper Alisson Becker, arguably Liverpool's best player, kept his side in the game, producing important saves to keep out Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton in a first half that also saw Palace hit the bar through Yeremy Pino. He finished with six saves.

Palace's hard work was undone by Quinten Timber losing Mac Allister at a free-kick five minutes before the break, allowing the Argentina international to head in his fifth goal of the season - as many as he managed in the entirety of last season.

articles.title: England await Guehi scan results after injury concern
articles.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi will undergo a scan on a hip complaint on Sunday to determine whether he can report for England duty this week.
body: The 26-year-old was substituted at half-time of City's loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and manager Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards the centre-back had requested to come off because of the injury.
Maresca did not specify Guehi's issue, but it is understood he has been troubled by the hip problem in recent weeks.
The fact he requested to be substituted has placed doubt over whether he will be available for England's Uefa Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.
Guehi will undergo tests, although it is likely England medical staff will also want to assess the player before a final decision is made.

articles.title: 'That's Reece' - World Cup semi-final brings out best and worst of Walsh
articles.summary: On a fractious night in Sydney that ended with Australia reaching yet another Men's Rugby League World Cup final, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh centre stage – for better or worse.
body: On a fractious night in Sydney, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh at the centre of the action – for better or worse.
The full-back scored three of Australia's eight tries as they beat Samoa 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final.
His two second-half tries helped keep a burgeoning Samoa comeback at bay, while his first-half effort demonstrated his skill and showmanship.
On 32 minutes, Walsh administered the harshest of punishments on Samoa for the smallest amount of defensive laxity, racing through the tiniest gap on the left to score.

articles.title: WWE Crown Jewel just made the case for Chelsea Green to win the 2027 Royal Rumble
articles.summary: Remember that ill-fated suggestion from “WWE Unreal” about Chelsea Green potentially winning the Rumble? After what just happened at Saturday's Crown Jewel, it might not be so far-fetched anymore.
body: Remember that ill-fated suggestion from the first season of “WWE Unreal” about Chelsea Green potentially winning the Royal Rumble? After what happened at t his weekend’s Crown Jewel, the result once touted as an out-there gambit (or “horrible option,” in the words of the WWE writers’ room) might not be as far-fetched as you think.

Sure, they’d be wise to drop the whole screwball comedy part about Green winning by default by being the last entrant when everyone else is already out. But the underlying idea of having one of pro-wrestling’s most compelling underdogs win the Rumble? That could turn out to be one of the single hottest cards in WWE’s deck right now.

We’ve known for months now that Chelsea Green has some off-the-charts babyface appeal. How about that five-star speech she delivered on “SmackDown” after Nick Aldis suggested she should vacate her first ever world title due to injury? The stirring segment in which Green fought back seemed to come from out of nowhere, and could end up going down in the history books as the best WWE promo of the year.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham Admits It’s Time to Panic
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham admits it's time to panic after Michigan's embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, calling the offensive performance three steps backward.
body: Things have officially gone from bad to worse for the Michigan Wolverines, and head coach Kyle Whittingham isn’t even trying to sugarcoat it anymore. Following Michigan’s embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State at the Big House on Saturday night, Whittingham made an admission that should have every Wolverines fan seriously concerned.
When asked whether it was time to panic about Michigan’s struggling offense, Whittingham offered a response that was as short as it was alarming.
That’s right, folks. The head coach of the Michigan Wolverines is now openly acknowledging that it’s time to panic about an offense that has been an absolute disaster throughout the 2026 season.

And unfortunately for Michigan fans, his comments only got more concerning from there. Whittingham didn’t make excuses, and he certainly didn’t attempt to convince anyone that Saturday’s performance was acceptable.

articles.title: Week 10 CFB Overreactions: Cash is still king, first-year coaches in trouble and Lane Kiffin's Alabama problem
articles.summary: Plus, why UCLA is more like 2024 Indiana than 2025's version and Missouri can't dodge the 'Paper Tiger' allegations after yet another loss to a ranked team
body: Big NIL spenders typically land the best transfer and recruiting classes. That talent typically leads to more wins, right? Yup. Turns out, most programs that spent a lot of money this fall haven't necessarily wasted their cash.

Twelve teams spent about $40 million on players this season, according to CBS Sports' reporting in the preseason. That's a nice number to start with in this 12-team playoff era, and unsurprisingly those rich programs are (mostly) winning more games.
Four others have three losses, and we suspect at least one of them will become the first three-loss team in the CFP: LSU, Ohio State, Oregon and Ole Miss.

The two remaining undefeated teams ( Utah and UCLA ) are not in the grouping, of course. And among the seven programs that spent $40 million or more, only two have one loss: Miami and Notre Dame, which met Saturday.
